request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted]
DOB: [redacted]
Admission Date: [redacted]
Discharge Date: [redacted]

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with complaints of headache and altered sensory perception. MRI images revealed gyriform enhancement with FLAIR hyperintensity and restricted diffusion in the right parietal cortex. The patient was found to have elevated protein and lymphocytic pleocytosis through CSF analysis. Additionally, the patient's glucose levels were elevated, and he was diagnosed with diabetes mellitus. The patient had spent significant time outdoors, including recent trips to Maine and New York, but had not reported any tick or mosquito bites. Serum was positive by JCV IgM ELISA with a PRNT of 1:160.

The patient remained in the hospital for observation and monitoring. The patient's headache and fatigue persisted over the next year, but repeat MRI 14 months later was normal. The patient was discharged with recommendations for outpatient follow-up appointments and further evaluation and monitoring as needed.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-Up:
It is recommended that the patient follow up with a neurologist for ongoing evaluation and monitoring. The patient should also continue following recommendations for diabetes management.

Discharge Medications:
N/A

Discharge Plan:
The patient was discharged in stable condition with recommendations for outpatient follow-up appointments. The patient should continue following recommendations for management of diabetes. Further evaluation and monitoring is recommended for ongoing neurological symptoms.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: A83**

The principal diagnosis is a mosquito-borne viral encephalitis, most likely Jamestown Canyon virus infection. The MRI findings (cortical enhancement, FLAIR hyperintensity, restricted diffusion), the CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis with elevated protein, and the positive serology (IgM ELISA with PRNT 1:160) together point to neuroinvasive arboviral disease. The travel history to Maine and New York fits the virus's geographic range. Jamestown Canyon virus is transmitted by mosquitoes, so the category is A83 (mosquito-borne viral encephalitis) rather than A84 (tick-borne) or A85 (other viral encephalitis).

The diabetes is a comorbidity and does not drive the admission. The record does not state the final diagnosis explicitly, so this assignment rests on the clinical findings described.
